---
title: "nota2md"
subtitle: "One legal provision of Mexico's official gazette, or one federal law, as Markdown"
toc: false
number-sections: false
---

::: {.home-lead}
**nota2md** builds the Markdown of a single legal provision of the *Diario
Oficial de la Federación* (DOF), identified by its `codNota`. When the
`scjn-leyes` release covers that `codNota`, the answer is the Supreme Court's
consolidated text of the whole law as it read right after that reform; when it
does not, the answer is the DOF's own text, converted from its HTML or, for the
scanned decades, OCR'd from its page images or PDF. The same package replays a
law's current text from nothing but its reform decrees, and matches each of the
Court's snapshots to the DOF note that produced it.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## The DOF is the official source; the SCJN is not

The gazette, read through [dofjson](https://legistlan.github.io/dofjson/), is
the official source of legal text. The Court's consolidated texts, read through
[scjn](https://legistlan.github.io/scjn/), are an editorial product over it: a
convenience corpus. Every file the SCJN path writes keeps its `fuente: scjn`
provenance header and lands under a different file name, so the file alone says
where it came from.
:::

::: {.fronts}
::: {.front}
### Three sources, one call

`legal_provisions(codNota)` answers from the SCJN corpus by default and falls
back to the DOF's HTML, images or PDF; `source="dof"` forces the original.
:::
::: {.front}
### The gazette side of the project

`nota2md.linking` is the one place that knows how an SCJN snapshot becomes a
`codNota`, and `reconstruct_legal_provisions` rebuilds a law from the DOF
alone.
:::
::: {.front}
### Five releases, two caches

`nota2md download all` puts the four SCJN releases and the gazette's archive
on disk, each in the cache of the package that owns it.
:::
:::

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install nota2md
nota2md download federal-laws --slug lfca    # the one law the examples use
nota2md 5788357                              # the law at that reform, from the SCJN
nota2md 4648702 --outdir output              # an ordinary decree, from the DOF's HTML
```

```python
from nota2md import legal_provisions, get_document, reconstruct_legal_provisions

legal_provisions(5788357)                     # -> <cache>/scjn-leyes/md/lfca-22-05-2026.md
legal_provisions(4648702, "output", source="dof")   # -> output/nota-4648702.md

documento = get_document(4648702)             # dofjson's record, cadenaContenido as Markdown
reconstruct_legal_provisions([5592105, 5730586], "output", nombre_ley="LEY de Amnistía")
```

See [Install](pages/install.qmd) for what the package needs and where it
writes, [Command line](pages/cli.qmd) and [Python](pages/python.qmd) for the
two ways to call it, [Sources](pages/sources.qmd) for how a note's text is
chosen and cut, [Linking](pages/linking.qmd) for how a snapshot gets its
`codNota`, [Reconstruction](pages/reconstruction.qmd) for the replay of a law's
decrees, [Releases](pages/releases.qmd) for the data it reads, and
[Scripts](pages/scripts.qmd) for the three scripts that maintain the corpus'
DOF side. Extending the package itself is documented separately, on the
[developer docs](https://legistlan.github.io/nota2md/dev/).
